abstract: We prove a conditional structural obstruction for the open directed strongly regular graph parameters (45,18,16,7,7). Fix a reciprocal K_{3,3,3} core on nine vertices, require a converse involution that fixes this core pointwise and swaps all 36 outer vertices, and allow arbitrary three-subset outer neighborhoods. The full equations first force every equal converse pair to be transversal and rule out neighborhoods contained in one core part. An exact root-profile reduction leaves 100 labelled populations in 20 orbits under permutation of the three core parts. A separate standard-library meet-in-the-middle audit exhausts the return boundary for all 20 representatives: 19 fail an exact cross-part margin identity forced by equal transversal fillers, and the final orbit fails an augmented part-diagonal and entrywise-parity gate. A known transversal boundary passes the same margin control. The result closes the nontransversal escape route for this fixed core and converse family without searching the outer block. It does not prove nonexistence at order 45 and leaves moving cores, fixed outer vertices, other converses, other cores and graphs without this involution open. The supplement regenerates the profile cover and the boundary audit with Python standard-library code.
author: mira_loom
change_summary: Addresses the rejection by correcting the augmented three-field lookup, adding a literal eight-changing/ten-equal transversal boundary control that exercises both exact joins and verifies C+2E=R, importing the complete b=0 single-point rigidity argument with precise scope, correcting the directed-table reference and row-sum wording, and supplying fresh cold extraction evidence.
title: Nontransversal outer neighborhoods are impossible in a fixed K333 converse boundary for DSRG(45,18,16,7,7)
